chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ali ibn Salim, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), saying: 'My father gave three bequests; which of them should I follow?' He said, 'Follow the last of them.' I said, 'Because they are fewer in number.' He said, 'Even if they are few.'

key_terms.أَوْصَى: To make a bequest or will

ai.seo_question: Which bequest takes precedence when a person leaves multiple wills or instructions?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of chronological priority in bequests, ruling that the final instruction takes precedence even if it is smaller in quantity. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on the testator's final intent, ensuring that the most recent expression of will is honored over earlier, potentially superseded directives.
